title: Elijah Carney balances football, academics, and faith at Middle Tennessee State University
text:
Elijah Carney, a senior linebacker for the Blue Raiders at Middle Tennessee State University, was recognized on May 13 as the Department of Philosophy and Religious Studies’ Outstanding Student of the Year and nominated for the College of Liberal Arts outstanding student award.
Carney’s achievements highlight his ability to manage both academic excellence and athletic commitments. He was inducted into Chi Alpha Sigma, a national honor society for student-athletes excelling in both sports and academics. Carney maintains a 4.0 GPA while majoring in philosophy and recently added religious studies as a second major.
“I’ve always been a thinker,” Carney said. “I read ‘The Confessions’ by St. Augustine in a class my freshman year and it just changed my perspective. I liked what he had to say.” After transferring from Bethel University in West Tennessee following his freshman year, Carney joined MTSU’s football team after meeting Coach Derek Mason during tryouts. “I applied here, got accepted, got introduced to Coach (Derek) Mason, went to a tryout, and made the team,” Carney said. “I was like, ‘Yeah, this is definitely going to be it.’ And I love Murfreesboro, too.”
Since joining MTSU in fall 2024, Carney has received several team honors such as Defensive Scout Team Player of the Week and Special Teams Scout Player of the Week recognition. AJ Reisig, linebacker coach for MTSU said: “Elijah is a person of exceptional character, as a student and as a teammate… He truly exemplifies what it means to be a student-athlete.” Reisig also said that Carney manages his workload with discipline: “He is able to manage the workload from both while giving maximum effort to whatever he is currently doing at the time… He has never allowed his circumstances to dictate or control his effort.”
Carney described balancing football with academics as challenging but manageable by taking things one day at a time: “That is a good question,” he said when asked how he manages everything. “I’m not even sure if I know how. It’s just a day at a time.” He credited football with teaching him resilience: “They always say ‘Control what you can control.’ There’s a lot of things that go on that I can’t control… But what can I do? And how can I react?”
Gregory Slack, assistant professor of philosophy who nominated Carney for outstanding student honors said: “What makes Elijah stand out as a student is his passion for philosophy and his excellent philosophical writing skills… His papers are always thoughtful, clearly written, well-argued and creative.” Slack noted that despite demanding schedules due to athletics commitments: “He always gets all required work done in timely manner.”
Outside academics and athletics responsibilities—where he leads Bible study groups—Carney remains active through Every Nation Campus ministry activities along with volunteer work supporting Boys & Girls Clubs locally.
Reflecting on receiving departmental recognition unexpectedly among peers whom he admires academically himself—”I was shocked for real,” Carney said—he continues focusing on personal growth within classroom settings alongside teammates on field while looking forward towards possible future ministry opportunities after graduation.
